title: Forest & Bird says personal data from website forms was accessed in a cyber incident
date_note: Published November 20; RNZ (via ODT) says Forest & Bird was alerted to the hack on Wednesday (18 November); the article does not say when the access began.
geo_basis: organisation country; Wellington used as the national point
summary: New Zealand conservation charity Forest & Bird told people that personal information they gave through a website form was accessed without authorisation. Names, phone numbers and email addresses were accessed, RNZ reported. Chief executive Sam Rowland said the group was alerted to the hack on Wednesday and a forensic search found malicious files hidden to read data; Police, the National Cyber Security Centre and the Privacy Commissioner were told. No number of people was given.
plain: A New Zealand conservation charity says hackers got names, phone numbers and email addresses that people entered on its website forms. Scam messages could follow.
exec: A well-known charity's supporter data was exposed; it shows how web form data can fuel convincing donation scams.
action: If you gave Forest & Bird details online, treat unexpected messages with caution; donations only via payments.forestandbird.org.nz and email only from @forestandbird.org.nz.
impact: Names, phone numbers and email addresses of people who used Forest & Bird website forms may be affected; the number is not stated.

validation.note: NZ Herald (20 Nov) quoting Forest & Bird email and Rowland; RNZ (Mary Argue, 20 Nov, via ODT) also reports the data types, Rowland quotes and notifications. An expert's guess about a criminal gang is not an attribution and is not recorded.
